The fracture toughness of silicide phases in the four alloys was evaluated in the 1000 nm indentations and the results are listed in Table 3 . It is interesting to note that the fracture toughness of both intermetallics was improved by the addition of Ga.
The fracture toughness of Nb 3Si was increased by 33.3% in the Nb e16Sie1Ga alloy compared to the Nb e16Si alloy.

Mechanistically, when an alloying element is added to an intermetallic there are two competing effects. First it increases the strength due to solid solution strengthening. Second and unique to intermetallics, the solute disrupts the order of the intermetallic compound.

Mechanistically, when an alloying element is added to an intermetallic there are two competing effects. First it increases the strength due to solid solution strengthening. Second and unique to intermetallics, the solute disrupts the order of the intermetallic compound. Disruption of the order makes plasticity occur much more easily because it decreases the energy of the anti-phase boundary that forms between the two halves of the super dislocations.
